A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research, despite the new DDB title. The main texts and complete supplementary materials are readable, with matching methods, original benchmarks, tables and figures supporting reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original evaluations on Waterbirds, CelebA and MetaShift, including pruning, sample-count and textual-inversion studies in Tables 1–5.

after.justification: V2 retains these original results and adds a two-class ImageNet-A experiment in supplementary Section 9.4.

M1.justification: The textual inversion, LangSAM masking, diffusion inpainting, softmax/Integrated Gradients pruning and weighted ERM retraining procedures remain unchanged. Equations (1)–(8) and Algorithms 1–2 are retained; adopting the DDB name does not change the method.

E1.justification: Section 9.4 adds a restricted cockroach/bee evaluation on ImageNet-A using ImageNet-1k training samples. This extends coverage to natural adversarial images while retaining the three original benchmarks and their tasks.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains DFR, JTT, AFR, MaskTune, LISA, DISC, DaC and ERM with the same participation across benchmarks. The added ImageNet-A experiment reuses ERM rather than introducing a new comparison method.

E3.justification: The new ImageNet-A experiment specifies SGD training at learning rate 0.001, Adam retraining at 0.0005, batch size 32 and both generated-sample weights equal to 1, evaluated by average accuracy. Settings, splits and metrics for the retained experiments are unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 9.4 adds a limited robustness check on naturally adversarial images beyond the original spurious-correlation benchmarks. The pruning, sample-count and textual-inversion studies, along with the existing masking and generation failure analyses, remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Table 1 retains the same mean-and-standard-deviation reporting over three retraining runs where available. The ImageNet-A addition supplies no run counts, seeds, uncertainty estimates or significance tests, so it establishes no new statistical reporting practice.

E6.justification: The retained numerical tables are unchanged. Section 9.4 newly reports 43.26% average accuracy for ERM versus 62.58% after DDB on two ImageNet-A classes; Figures 9–15 add generated-image examples. These are additional results, not same-setting performance improvements over v1.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and Equations (1)–(8) are retained, and neither version supplies theorems or proofs. The new SCM/backdoor-path remark in Section 3 provides conceptual interpretation without developing a formal causal model or derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the claims about automated minority-sample generation, pruning, improved group robustness and potential applicability to data scarcity. Naming the method DDB and adding supporting experiments do not materially change these claims.

C2.justification: Section 3 adds an SCM/backdoor-path interpretation to the earlier correlation-based explanation. Supplementary Section 9.2 more explicitly describes minority-token selection as preventing reconstruction of majority spurious features. The stated dependence on diffusion/segmentation capabilities and misuse limitations remain substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: The abstract newly states code availability and supplies a repository link. Section 9.4 documents the added experiment's training source, optimizers, learning rates, batch size and loss weights. Existing implementation references, hardware/timing information and Table 10 hyperparameters are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations to ImageNet, Natural Adversarial Examples and Pearl's Causality, supporting the new experiment and causal framing. The related-work discussion and positioning relative to existing methods otherwise remain unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 adopts the DDB title and terminology, updates affiliation/contact text, makes localized explanatory edits, and adds acknowledgments and two supplementary subsections. Most prose and section ordering remain intact. Section 3 introduces the unfinished phrase 'Structrul Causal We consider'.

P2.justification: Figures 9–15 substantially expand the qualitative presentation with initial-image/mask/generated-image comparisons for ImageNet-A and both conversion directions across the original datasets. Figures 1–8 remain unchanged, and Table 2 renames its NoPruning column. The new CelebA captions confusingly describe gender-class changes despite the stated hair-color task.

improvement.justification: V2 adds useful, limited evidence beyond the original benchmarks, documents the new experiment's settings, and provides a code-access link and more inspectable generation examples. The gain is modest: ImageNet-A covers only two classes without uncertainty reporting, while unfinished causal-model prose and misleading CelebA captions reduce clarity. These localized defects temper the added empirical support and reproducibility information.
